entries.name: numeric-receiver-width-spend-n0#0
entries.description: [N0] `sigmaProp(row == row)` around `SLong.toBytes on Long 1` guards the box being SPENT. THE CONTROL: the call is well-formed, so both operands evaluate, the script reduces to true and the box SPENDS. It is what makes the invalid rows about the operand's width rather than about the wrapper or the carrier.

entries.name: numeric-receiver-width-spend-n1#1
entries.description: [N1] `sigmaProp(row == row)` around `SLong.toBytes on Int 1` guards the box being SPENT. **THE SEPARATING ROW.** The box parses and a node carries it, so ANYONE CAN CREATE it. On the JVM the left operand throws `ClassCastException` to `java.lang.Long` (the handler casts the receiver to the owner's class) and the spend is INVALID. An evaluator that computes at the operand's width returns a value, and `x == x` is true for any value it returns, so it lets a spender TAKE the box: an over-accept on reachable state.

expected.reason: org.ergoplatform.validation.MalformedModifierError: Scripts of all transaction inputs should pass verification. 8f306620333be3a73142e6798fc7857394a925590242e00edcda9895f50065c4: #0 => Failure(java.lang.ClassCastException: class java.lang.Integer cannot be cast to class java.lang.Long (java.lang.Integer and java.lang.Long are in module java.base of loader 'bootstrap'))
